label: D1 after a common a1->S1 trial, growing exponentially late in episode; unrewarded > rewarded
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/12) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1) * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/12) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 r") * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/12) ;; (phase == D1) * last_is("a1 S1 u") * np.exp((ep_trial-99)/12)
explanation: Fires only at D1, with magnitude rising roughly as exp((ep_trial-99)/12) toward the end of the episode. The additive timing baseline averages over previous trials; the real structure is multiplicative: the late-episode ramp applies only when the previous trial was a1 -> S1 (common). It is larger after a1 S1 unrewarded (weight +3.3) than after a1 S1 rewarded (+2.6). After a trial that reached S2 (-1.24) or a rare a2 -> S1 (-0.98), it is pushed down to about zero. Four observed-only terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.74 (dev 0.75), well above the additive all-cue ceiling of 0.24, because the cues interact with episode time. Small leftover structure: it can stay high after an a2 S1 trial when earlier trials were a1 S1, and on window-first trials. The trial before (tv state/action -2) adds about 0.001; the D1 policy logit adds about 0.025 (model output, not recorded). Value, hidden good state and this trial reward add essentially nothing. GO and D2 are always 0.

issues: Minor: the 'unrewarded > rewarded' distinction is real in direction (D1 residual after a1 S1 u is +0.43 vs +0.28 after a1 S1 r; fitted weights 3.28 vs 2.58), but it adds only about 0.004 of test R^2. Using one a1 S1 term without the reward split gives 0.740 vs 0.744.

Minor: the exp((ep_trial-99)/12) ramp under-predicts the plateau at roughly t89-95 (actual about 3.0-3.5 vs predicted 2.1-2.9 in the worst-fit windows). Other shapes do not beat it, though: scale 8 gives 0.697, 18 gives 0.721, 25 gives 0.659, and a sigmoid centred at 85 gives 0.739.

Minor: the leftover structure the explanation admits to (high activation after a2 S1 when the trial before was a1 S1, and on the window's first trial where prev_* = -1) shows up in the worst-fit windows, but targeted terms recover only about 0.005 (0.7489 with 4 extra terms). The largest mean error in any phase x previous-trial cell is +0.045, so no large systematic error class remains.

The claims check out: activation is 0 at GO and D2 (timing baseline and residuals are 0 there); the ramp is a late-episode effect; S2 and a2->S1 previous trials are suppressed about equally (merging them costs 0.003); the terms use no future variables; adding the hidden good state x a1 S1 interaction adds nothing (0.743).
